newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour won't turn clock back for trades unions.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour won't turn clock back for trades unions.

text.p: Britain's main opposition Labour Party has no intention of undoing most of the recent reforms of trades union legislation if it wins the May 1 election, trade and industry spokeswoman Margaret Beckett said on Monday.
"There is no question of returning to a closed shop or compulsory union membership," Beckett said on BBC Television.
But Beckett said the pendulum had now swung too far the other way.
"In a free society people should be free to belong to a union and at the moment they're not," she said.
Beckett said she was a still a Socialist but this was not incompatible with being enthusiastic about business and free trade.
"Socialism, which is a creed which aims to help the many not the few, can propsper best in a delivering economy," she said.
Asked whether she still believed in redistribution of wealth, Beckett said: "I believe in making it first and then we can discuss how it can better be spread."
